title: Comprehension as an Architectural Characteristic: A System That Is Not Understood Cannot Evolve Safely
gist: Four architects from the InfoQ Certified Architect Program argue that human comprehension is an architectural characteristic that decays silently, and that GenAI - by compressing the 'execute' layer that used to build mental models for free - has made comprehension debt the fastest-growing liability in software. Their prescription is stretched fitness functions (blocking oversized PRs, CodeOwners forbidding agent-only review, Degree of Authorship / git-truck knowledge maps, ADR checks on core-boundary PRs) plus a reframing of human review as a comprehension checkpoint rather than a quality gate, with design reviews outranking code reviews in agentic flows.

insights.claim: Human comprehension of a system should be treated as a first-class architectural characteristic alongside performance and availability, because unlike those it decays silently and a system that is not understood cannot evolve safely.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Reframes an unpriced operational risk: firms shipping AI-generated code may be accruing an invisible liability that only surfaces during incidents or migrations.
insights.quote: Unlike characteristics like performance and availability, this property can deteriorate silently over time, and a system that is not understood cannot evolve safely.
insights.locator: Key Takeaways

insights.claim: Peter Naur's 'Programming as Theory Building' is used as the load-bearing premise that a system includes the mental model held by its programmers and not just the code, which makes how widely and durably that theory is held across a team a property of the system itself.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: If theory is part of the asset, technical due diligence and acquisition analysis should weight team continuity, not just repo quality.
insights.quote: His claim is that the system includes the theory and not just the code.
insights.locator: In evolutionary architecture, systems should be

insights.claim: Margaret-Anne Storey's taxonomy splits system debt into three kinds - technical, cognitive (the silent loss of shared understanding) and intent (the lack of rationale for why the system is the way it is) - and comprehension is positioned as the direct antidote to the latter two.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Gives a vocabulary for auditing engineering orgs beyond code metrics; tooling that instruments cognitive/intent debt addresses a newly named category.
insights.quote: she defines three distinct kinds of system debt: technical, cognitive and intent
insights.locator: Margaret-Anne Storey expands on this idea

insights.claim: Comprehension debt is defined as the gap between what the system is and what the team understands it to be, and is framed as a liability that accrues interest and cannot be paid down in a single effort - only recurring habits work.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Argues against one-off documentation sprints or knowledge-transfer projects as fixes; process change, not a project, is the only remedy.
insights.quote: comprehension debt (the gap between what the system is and what the team understands it to be) is a liability that accrues interest
insights.locator: If comprehension is an architectural characteristic

themes.theme: Three Erosion Forces: Fragmentation, Churn, GenAI

insights.claim: Three forces erode system comprehension at different speeds - knowledge fragmentation, team churn, and AI-generated change - and none announces itself because the system keeps passing all its automated gates while the underlying theory thins.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Green CI dashboards and passing SLOs are not evidence of organizational health; leading indicators must be watched instead.
insights.quote: the system keeps passing its gates while the theory behind it thins unseen
insights.locator: Fragmentation, churn, and generative AI each widen

insights.claim: Decentralized architectural decision-making optimizes flow and builds deep local sub-domain expertise but fragments the global picture, so teams keep how their service works while losing the why behind where systemic boundaries were drawn.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: A named cost against the popular team-autonomy and microservices playbook; without shared governance, local theories drift apart.
insights.quote: Teams may understand how their service works, yet could lose the "why" behind where the systemic boundaries were drawn in the first place.
insights.locator: In complex systems maintained by multiple teams

insights.claim: New hires who lack the historical context of why boundaries exist fall back on tactical patches rather than systemic improvements matching the original design, which erodes architectural integrity - because existing artifacts generally record the what and not the why.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: High-attrition engineering orgs compound architectural decay non-linearly; retention and rationale-capture are architectural controls, not just HR line items.
insights.quote: aided by artifacts that generally record the what and not the why
insights.locator: Team churn also compounds this problem

insights.claim: GenAI is identified as the latest and fastest erosion force precisely because it removed the implementation effort that used to build developers' mental models of the system as a free byproduct of design, implementation and verification.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: The productivity gain from AI coding tools is partly funded by an unbooked comprehension cost; ROI claims that ignore it are overstated.
insights.quote: It reduced the implementation effort that used to generate comprehension as a byproduct, but that effort was also what built the mental model of the system in developers.
insights.locator: The latest and fastest of these three forces is GenAI

insights.claim: A first-hand anecdote describes an experienced engineer spending considerable time during a client feature demo to understand code she had shipped a week earlier, because she had never formed a mental model of it despite the code passing every quality gate.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence that today's quality gates are blind to comprehension loss - a leading signal for where AI-code-governance tooling demand emerges.
insights.quote: The code passed every quality gate, but the demo was the first time the comprehension debt surfaced.
insights.locator: During a feature demo to a client

insights.claim: Comprehension cannot be measured directly, so the prescription is to monitor leading indicators of its decay using fitness functions deliberately stretched to assess the sociotechnical system around the code, only some of which are fully automatable.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: A concrete instrumentation blueprint that engineering-analytics and DevEx vendors could productize.
insights.quote: So, we have deliberately stretched the term.
insights.locator: Detecting and Measuring Comprehension Loss

insights.claim: The governance rule offered for people-metrics is to enforce only when gaming is hard or harmless and to monitor otherwise, treating thresholds as triggers for investigation rather than targets, because a gate that blocks a PR can simply be gamed.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: A portable heuristic for any org rolling out DORA-style or AI-usage metrics; misapplied enforcement produces gaming, not improvement.
insights.quote: enforce when gaming is hard or harmless and monitor otherwise
insights.locator: Metrics about people change behavior when enforced

insights.claim: Two controls are recommended as hard enforcement: blocking pull requests too large to review, and using policies such as CodeOwners to ensure an agentic code reviewer is never the sole reviewer - it can be first, but a human must follow.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: A concrete policy pattern that caps how far AI code review can substitute for humans - a ceiling on the addressable market for fully autonomous review tools.
insights.quote: Do not let agentic code reviews be the sole reviewer of the PR - they can be the first reviewer, but it has to be followed by a human reviewer.
insights.locator: Agentic Code Reviewer

insights.claim: Review dysfunction should be tracked as the share of approved PRs with no substantive comments or only 'LGTM' plus the distribution of reviews across the team, with remediation being reviewer rotation and making it explicit that challenging any author's design is expected, including the architect's.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: A cheap telemetry cut available today from any VCS dataset, and a direct read on whether approvals are real signal or formality.
insights.quote: Track the share of approved PRs having no substantive comments or with only ‘LGTM’, and the distribution of reviews across the team.
insights.locator: Review Dysfunction

insights.claim: Degree of Authorship (DOA) and a low truck factor are proposed as knowledge-concentration signals, monitorable with tools like git-truck that map knowledge distribution across a codebase and expose severe single points of failure, with the caveat that DOA is only one imperfect signal.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Names an actual tool for quantifying key-person risk in a repo - directly usable in technical due diligence.
insights.quote: Monitor it using tools like git-truck that can map knowledge distribution across a codebase and expose severe single points of failure.
insights.locator: Knowledge Distribution

insights.claim: Onboarding should be measured as the time until a new hire contributes to the design and architecture of the system rather than time to first pull request, and rising onboarding time is treated as a direct proxy for cognitive overhead weighing on tenured engineers too.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Redefines a widely tracked DevEx metric in a way that would make many orgs' fast-onboarding claims look far worse.
insights.quote: Track the time it takes for the new hire to contribute to the design and architecture of the system, not just raise pull requests.
insights.locator: Onboarding Friction

insights.claim: Intent-documentation decay is detectable by flagging PRs that touch core or structural boundaries without adding an ADR or rationale documentation, with the practical test for whether to document being whether someone who wasn't here would need it.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Converts a vague documentation mandate into a specific, automatable pipeline signal.
insights.quote: Monitor the origin of such issues by detecting when a PR touches core or structural boundaries without adding an ADR or documentation for the rationale.
insights.locator: Lack of Documentation of Intent

insights.claim: Domain leakage - changes that degrade architectural boundaries so that local reasoning becomes impossible and isolated changes cause side effects elsewhere - is one of the few indicators that should hard-fail the build via architectural fitness functions.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Marks the boundary between what should be automated enforcement and what must stay human judgment in AI-era pipelines.
insights.quote: Use architectural fitness functions to fail the build if constraints are violated
insights.locator: Domain Leakage

insights.claim: Design reviews are prescribed for any change with a large blast radius touching the essentially complex core or seams regardless of change size, and because this is hard to enforce, teams should track core-module PRs merged without a prior design review and require a catch-up team session from the author.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: A specific, auditable compensating control for orgs where small AI-generated diffs quietly touch critical modules.
insights.quote: Code changes with a large blast radius - the essentially complex core and seams - should always be preceded by a design review, regardless of the size of the change.
insights.locator: Missing Design Reviews

themes.theme: Pre-hoc vs Post-hoc Comprehension in Agentic Flows

insights.claim: The central contrarian claim is that because AI has commoditized code generation, comprehension must now be sought before generation rather than during review, which makes design reviews more important than code reviews in agentic engineering flows.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Inverts the prevailing 'AI writes, humans review' operating model that most enterprise AI-coding rollouts are built on.
insights.quote: This is why design reviews are more important than code reviews in agentic engineering flows.
insights.locator: Comprehension Checkpoint

insights.claim: If design decisions are not made upfront, the system converges on the statistically default design the LLM was trained on rather than the one the specific business context demands, since there are numerous ways any system could be built.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Predicts homogenization of enterprise architectures under heavy AI codegen - a systemic risk and a differentiation opportunity for firms that resist it.
insights.quote: you will end up with a statistically default design that the LLM was trained on, not the one your context demands
insights.locator: Post-hoc comprehension implies that you will no longer

insights.claim: Human review in an agentic flow is reframed as a comprehension checkpoint rather than a quality gate: automated feedback sensors like fitness functions catch bad output, while the human's job is to hold the intent and build the theory of what the change does and why.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Changes what reviewer headcount is actually for; org designs that cut reviewers because AI reviews code are optimizing the wrong function.
insights.quote: The human review at this stage is a comprehension checkpoint, not a quality gate.
insights.locator: Comprehension Checkpoint

insights.claim: A concrete cheap probe for comprehension is having the engineer explain the code in their own words and manually write the PR description and merge commit message, because the friction of writing it reveals whether the author holds the theory - the value is destroyed if an agent generates it automatically.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: A zero-cost practice with a sharp implication: auto-generated PR summaries, a standard AI dev-tool feature, actively destroy the diagnostic signal.
insights.quote: The friction of writing the message is the probe for the author to find out if they hold the theory or not.
insights.locator: Have the engineer explain the code in their own words

insights.claim: The framework is explicitly selective rather than universal: grunt work can still be delegated to AI with the reviewer knowing just enough to verify output, and teams must decide when to hold the theory for the essentially complex core and when to let go.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Keeps the thesis from being a blanket anti-AI position and gives a triage rule - core and seams get human theory, everything else gets delegated.
insights.quote: Decide when to hold the theory for the essentially complex core, and when to let go.
insights.locator: This does not mean that every change has to follow

insights.claim: Before agents are allowed to code, requirements should be validated as unambiguous and testable with documented acceptance criteria - explicitly framed as not big upfront design because the unit is a single user story, not the entire system.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: The bottleneck in agentic delivery shifts from coding capacity to requirements clarity - relevant to where spend and tooling go next.
insights.quote: This is not a call for big upfront design, as the unit here is a user story and not the entire system.
insights.locator: Teams should start by validating the requirements

insights.claim: The 'decide-execute-deliver' sandwich model attributed to Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor is used to argue that generative AI compressed only the middle execute layer, so the comprehension that used to arise across all three layers must now be deliberately created at the two ends.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: A clean mental model of where AI actually captures value in the software workflow - and where human labor does not compress.
insights.quote: Generative AI has compressed the middle layer, and we argue that the comprehension that used to come in all three layers should now be deliberately created at the two ends.
insights.locator: A recent article from Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor

insights.claim: Active problem-solving without a ready-made solution is claimed to produce context-relevant, creative designs, whereas passive reading of already-generated code does not - so if code review and verification are the only places comprehension is sought, comprehension never actually forms.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: A mechanism-level argument for why AI-assisted teams can appear productive while structurally losing design capability.
insights.quote: If code reviews and verification are the only places where our comprehension is sought, then comprehension never really forms.
insights.locator: There is a core difference in an engineer understanding a module

themes.theme: Sustaining the Shared Model at Seams

insights.claim: Individual comprehension is necessary but insufficient: divergence inside one engineer's head is cheap to fix, but divergence of mental models across communicating sub-systems and teams is expensive, making bounded context seams the most important place to share understanding.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Tells you where to spend scarce architectural attention - at integration seams, not uniformly across the codebase.
insights.quote: But when sub-systems communicate, and different teams interact, the divergence of mental models is expensive.
insights.locator: Sustaining the Shared Model

insights.claim: An API schema documents request/response shape, pre-conditions and authorization but omits the behavioral contract - idempotency, retry-safety, ordering requirements, consistency and delivery guarantees - and that behavior is theory that must exist on both sides of the boundary.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Explains why schema-first tooling and contract specs alone do not prevent integration failures; a visible gap in the contract-testing tool category.
insights.quote: does not talk about the behavioral aspect of the contract - things like idempotency, retry-safety, ordering requirements, consistency, and delivery guarantees
insights.locator: An API schema, for example, explains the shape

insights.claim: ADRs and context maps are declared necessary but insufficient because artifacts do not sustain comprehension by themselves; only knowledge flow does, via deliberate team topologies, pairing, rotating engineers across modules, and decentralized architectural decision-making.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Deflates documentation tooling as the solution and redirects spend toward organizational design.
insights.quote: Tools and artifacts such as ADRs and context maps are necessary, but they don’t sustain comprehension by themselves.
insights.locator: That shared model can be achieved only by enabling

insights.claim: With agents producing code faster than humans can comprehend, knowledge flow gains an additional first hop from agent to individual, and the person directing the agent must explain the design by reconciling what was implemented against the mental model they held during design, not by learning it from the generated output.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Names the specific new failure mode of agentic engineering and the specific behavior that mitigates it - a testable practice for teams scaling AI codegen.
insights.quote: The person directing the agent must be able to explain the design - not by learning it from the generated output, but by reconciling what was implemented with the mental model they had during design.
insights.locator: With GenAI, the knowledge silo issues are magnified

insights.claim: The cheap remediation window closes at production: discovering the comprehension gap only after agent-generated code is live means the cheap option has already been lost, so comprehension must be made deliberate at the seams, the core domains, and wherever the system should be evolvable.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: Frames comprehension work as buying optionality - an argument sized in option value and incident cost rather than developer sentiment.
insights.quote: If you discover the gap in comprehension only after the agent-generated code is in production, you've already lost the cheap option.
insights.locator: Engineering Comprehension Deliberately

insights.claim: Comprehension practices should be designed for the engineer who has not joined the team yet, meaning they must be baked into recurring process rather than depending on the tenure or memory of current staff.
insights.speaker: Jacobus Meintjes
insights.so_what: A durable design test for any knowledge-management investment: if it only serves current staff, it will not survive churn.
insights.quote: comprehension must be baked into the process in such a way that it is meant for the engineer who hasn’t joined yet
insights.locator: Like technical debt, it is not paid down in a single effort
